question: Who is the first Indian President to be born in Independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Droupadi Murmu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Droupadi Murmu (born 20 June 1958) became the 15th President of India, sworn in on 25 July 2022.

 

• She is the first person born in independent India (after 15 August 1947) to hold the office of President.

 

• She is also the first tribal (Santhal community) President of India and only the second woman President, after Pratibha Patil.

 

• She hails from Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, and earlier served as Governor of Jharkhand (2015–2021).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ram Nath Kovind (14th President, 2017–2022) preceded her; his term ended on 24 July 2022.

 

• Pratibha Patil was the 12th President (2007–2012) and Pranab Mukherjee the 13th President (2012–2017).

 

NOTE

 

• Ram Nath Kovind (Option 1): 14th President of India (2017–2022); born in 1945, before independence.

 

• Pratibha Patil (Option 3): 12th President of India (2007–2012), first woman President; born in 1934.

 

• Pranab Mukherjee (Option 4): 13th President of India (2012–2017); born in 1935.

question: Which of the following combinations of tenors of Treasury bills issued by Government of India is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 91 days, 182 days, 364 days.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Treasury Bills (T-Bills) are short-term money market instruments issued by the Government of India to meet short-term borrowing needs (राजकोष बिल — अल्पकालिक सरकारी प्रतिभूति).

 

• The RBI issues T-Bills in three standard tenors: 91 days, 182 days, and 364 days.

 

• T-Bills are zero-coupon instruments — issued at a discount to face value and redeemed at par, with the difference being the investor's return.

 

• They are sold through periodic auctions conducted by the RBI on behalf of the Government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• T-Bills are distinct from dated Government Securities (G-Secs), which have longer maturities.

 

• The minimum investment amount in T-Bills is Rs 25,000, and in multiples thereof.

 

NOTE

 

• 82 days, 182 days, 345 days (Option 1): Not the actual tenors issued; 82 and 345 days are not standard T-Bill maturities.

 

• 91 days, 152 days, 356 days (Option 2): Only the 91-day tenor is correct here; 152 and 356 days are not actual T-Bill maturities.

 

• 61 days, 145 days, 360 days (Option 4): None of these match the actual RBI-issued T-Bill tenors.

question: Wages/day under Mahatma Gandhi NREGA is ______, w.e.f. 1st April, 2020, as per Economic Survey 2020-21.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rs 202.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Economic Survey 2020-21, the all-India average wage rate under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was revised to Rs 202 per day, effective from 1st April 2020 (मनरेगा — महात्मा गांधी राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण रोजगार गारंटी अधिनियम).

 

• MGNREGA, enacted in 2005, guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.

 

• Wage rates are revised annually and vary state-wise, based on the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• MGNREGA is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

 

• The scheme was originally called NREGA (2005) and was renamed MGNREGA in 2009.

 

NOTE

 

• Rs 152 (Option 1): Not the revised all-India average wage figure cited for FY 2020-21.

 

• Rs 182 (Option 3): Incorrect figure; does not match the Economic Survey 2020-21 data.

 

• Rs 412 (Option 4): Far higher than the actual MGNREGA wage rate as per the Economic Survey.

question: India’s National Air Sports Policy was released in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Air Sports Policy (NASP) 2022 was launched by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 7 June 2022, unveiled by Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia.

 

• Its objective is to make India one of the top air sports nations by 2030, covering activities such as aeromodelling, ballooning, drone sports, gliding, hang gliding, paragliding, and skydiving.

 

• The policy provides for an autonomous apex body, the Air Sports Federation of India (ASFI), to regulate and promote air sports in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A draft of the policy was released earlier for public consultation before the final NASP 2022 was launched.

 

• The policy also aims to position India as a hub for air-sports tourism.

 

NOTE

 

• 2012 (Option 1): No dedicated national air sports policy existed at this time.

 

• 2000 (Option 2): Predates the formulation of any national air sports policy in India.

 

• 2016 (Option 4): Incorrect year; the policy was actually released in 2022.

question: What is the full form of FTP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is File transfer protocol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is a standard network protocol used to transfer computer files between a client and a server over a network.

 

• It operates on a client-server model, typically using TCP port 21 for control commands and port 20 for data transfer.

 

• FTP supports both anonymous access and authenticated (username/password) access.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Secure variants include FTPS (FTP over SSL/TLS) and SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol).

 

• Other common internet protocols include HTTP (web pages) and SMTP (email).

 

NOTE

 

• File transfer paging (Option 1): Not a real computing term or protocol.

 

• File text paging (Option 3): Not a real computing term or protocol.

 

• File text protocol (Option 4): Not a real computing term or protocol.

question: Sheetal wants to create financial statements for her business. Which among the following software should she use for the same?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spread sheet software.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Spreadsheet software (e.g., MS Excel, Google Sheets) organizes data into rows and columns and supports formulas, functions, and automatic calculations — ideal for preparing financial statements such as balance sheets, profit & loss accounts, and budgets.

 

• It allows formatting, sorting, charting, and analysis of numerical/financial data.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Popular spreadsheet software includes Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc, and Apple Numbers.

 

NOTE

 

• Presentation software (Option 1): Used to create slideshows (e.g., MS PowerPoint), not for financial calculations.

 

• System software (Option 2): Manages computer hardware and resources (e.g., operating systems); not designed for financial statements.

 

• Multimedia software (Option 3): Used to create/edit audio, video, and images; not suited to financial statement preparation.

question: Which among the following festivals is celebrated as the Telugu New Year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ugadi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ugadi (also called Yugadi) is celebrated as the Telugu and Kannada New Year, marking the start of the traditional lunisolar calendar (उगादी — तेलुगु नववर्ष).

 

• It falls on the first day of the Chaitra month (typically March/April) and is celebrated mainly in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.

 

• A special dish called "Ugadi Pachadi", combining six different tastes, is prepared to symbolise the varied experiences of life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same day is celebrated as Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra and Cheti Chand by the Sindhi community.

 

NOTE

 

• Dasara (Option 1): A major Hindu festival celebrating the victory of good over evil, not specifically the Telugu New Year.

 

• Vishu (Option 2): Celebrated as the traditional New Year in Kerala.

 

• Monpa (Option 4): Not a festival; the Monpa are a tribal community found in Arunachal Pradesh.

question: In 1757, ______ led the Company’s army against Sirajuddaulah at Plassey.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Clive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1757, Robert Clive led the forces of the British East India Company against Nawab Sirajuddaulah of Bengal in the Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757) (प्लासी का युद्ध).

 

• The battle was won largely due to the treachery of Mir Jafar, Sirajuddaulah's commander-in-chief, who withheld his forces from fighting.

 

• Victory at Plassey laid the foundation of British political power in Bengal, and eventually in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Robert Clive later became the first British Governor of Bengal.

 

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) further consolidated British control, leading to the grant of Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha in 1765.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 1): Governor-General of India (1786–1793); introduced the Permanent Settlement, not present at Plassey.

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 3): First Governor-General of Bengal (1772–1785); not involved at Plassey.

 

• Lord Minto (Option 4): Served as Governor-General of India in the early 1800s/1900s; unrelated to the Battle of Plassey.

question: Breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid and energy in lack of oxygen takes place in which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Human muscle cells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In humans, when oxygen supply is insufficient during vigorous exercise, muscle cells undergo anaerobic respiration (lactic acid fermentation), breaking down pyruvate into lactic acid, releasing a small amount of energy.

 

• This build-up of lactic acid in muscles causes fatigue and cramps.

 

• In contrast, yeast undergoes anaerobic respiration via alcoholic fermentation, converting pyruvate into ethanol and carbon dioxide, not lactic acid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aerobic respiration (with oxygen) occurs in the mitochondria and yields far more ATP than anaerobic respiration.

 

• Lactic acid accumulated in muscles is later converted back to glucose in the liver via the Cori cycle.

 

NOTE

 

• Bacteria (Option 1): Some bacteria do produce lactic acid, but this is not the standard textbook example being tested here.

 

• Mitochondria (Option 2): The site of aerobic respiration, not anaerobic lactic acid fermentation.

 

• Yeast (Option 3): Undergoes alcoholic fermentation (producing ethanol and CO2), not lactic acid fermentation.

question: Fourth edition of Khelo India Youth Games was hosted by which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 4th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2021 was hosted in Panchkula, Haryana, held from 4 to 13 June 2022 (delayed due to COVID-19).

 

• Haryana topped the medal tally at this edition.

 

• Khelo India Youth Games, launched in 2018, is an annual multi-sport event for young athletes aimed at promoting a grassroots sports culture in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• 1st edition (2018): New Delhi; 2nd edition (2019): Pune, Maharashtra; 3rd edition (2020): Guwahati, Assam.

 

• The 5th edition (Khelo India Youth Games 2022) was held in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh (January–February 2023).

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Hosted the 5th edition, not the 4th.

 

• Assam (Option 2): Hosted the 3rd edition (2020) in Guwahati.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Has not hosted any of these numbered editions of the Khelo India Youth Games.

question: Which continent provides more than half of world’s tin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asia produces more than half of the world's tin, with major producers including China, Indonesia, Myanmar, and Malaysia.

 

• China and Indonesia together rank as the two largest tin-producing countries in the world.

 

• Tin is primarily extracted from the mineral cassiterite (tinstone), often found in alluvial deposits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tin is chiefly used for tin-plating (e.g., tin cans) and in alloys such as bronze and solder.

 

• Other notable tin producers outside Asia include Peru and Bolivia (South America) and the Democratic Republic of Congo (Africa).

 

NOTE

 

• Europe (Option 1): Not a major tin-producing continent.

 

• North Africa (Option 2): Contributes negligibly to global tin output.

 

• Africa (Option 4): Contributes some tin (e.g., DR Congo, Nigeria), but far less than Asia's share.

question: Each orbit of International Space Station (ISS) takes ______ minutes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 90 – 93.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Space Station (ISS) orbits Earth at an average altitude of about 400 km, completing one orbit roughly every 90–93 minutes.

 

• This means the ISS completes about 15–16 orbits of Earth every day, so astronauts on board witness about 15–16 sunrises and sunsets daily.

 

• The ISS is a joint project of NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, and CSA, and has been continuously occupied since November 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ISS travels at a speed of about 28,000 km/h.

 

• India is separately developing its own future space station, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.

 

NOTE

 

• 80 – 82 (Option 1): Too short a range for the actual ISS orbital period.

 

• 85 – 87 (Option 2): Close but not the accepted range for the ISS orbital period.

 

• 83 – 86 (Option 4): Incorrect; the actual orbital period is closer to 90–93 minutes.

question: Which of the following pressure belt is known as the horse latitude?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sub - Tropical High Pressure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sub-Tropical High-Pressure belt, located around 30°–35° N and S latitudes, is also known as the "Horse Latitudes."

 

• The name is believed to have originated from becalmed sailing ships in these latitudes, where sailors sometimes threw horses overboard to conserve water and food during voyages delayed by weak, unpredictable winds.

 

• This belt is characterised by descending air, calm winds, and dry conditions, giving rise to many of the world's major deserts, such as the Sahara.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Equatorial Low-Pressure belt is also known as the Doldrums.

 

• The Sub-Polar Low-Pressure belt lies around 60°–65° N/S latitudes.

 

NOTE

 

• Equatorial Low Pressure (Option 1): Known as the Doldrums, not the horse latitudes.

 

• Sub - Polar Low Pressure (Option 2): Located near 60°–65° latitude, unrelated to the horse latitudes.

 

• High Pressure (Option 3): Too generic a term; not the specific name for the horse latitudes.

question: _________is the highest peak in the Eastern Ghats.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahendragiri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahendragiri (1,501 m), located in the Gajapati district of Odisha, is conventionally cited in Indian geography as the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats (महेंद्रगिरी — पूर्वी घाट की सबसे ऊँची चोटी).

 

• The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range of hills running along India's eastern coast from Odisha through Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu into parts of Karnataka, generally lower and more broken than the Western Ghats.

 

• Mahendragiri also holds religious/mythological significance, being mentioned in the Ramayana and Mahabharata as an abode associated with Parashurama.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A 2011 survey identified Jindhagada Peak (1,690 m) in the Araku Valley, Andhra Pradesh, as an even higher point of the Eastern Ghats; however, it is not among the given options, so Mahendragiri remains the standard exam answer.

 

NOTE

 

• Khasi (Option 2): The Khasi Hills are part of the Meghalaya Plateau in Northeast India, unrelated to the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Kanchenjunga (Option 3): The third-highest mountain in the world, part of the Himalayas, on the India–Nepal border.

 

• Anai Mudi (Option 4): The highest peak of the Western Ghats (and of Peninsular India), located in Kerala.

question: Which among the following corridors was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahakal Lok Corridor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Mahakal Lok Corridor (Sri Mahakaleshwar Temple Corridor) in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, on 11 October 2022 (महाकाल लोक — उज्जैन).

 

• It is a major redevelopment project around the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, featuring sculptures and murals depicting Shiva's life along with a grand entrance plaza.

 

• The corridor was developed to boost religious tourism infrastructure in Ujjain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mahakaleshwar Temple is also famous for its Bhasma Aarti, a unique ritual performed with sacred ash.

 

• The project is comparable in concept to the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi.

 

NOTE

 

• Kashi Corridor (Option 2): The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi was inaugurated earlier, in December 2021, not October 2022.

 

• Chennai Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (Option 3): An industrial infrastructure development project, not a corridor inaugurated by PM Modi in October 2022 in this context.

 

• North East Economic Corridor (Option 4): Not a project inaugurated by PM Modi in October 2022.

question: Which of the following is mentioned in state list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Betting and gambling.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Betting and gambling" is Entry 34 of the State List (List II) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, giving State legislatures exclusive power to legislate on it.

 

• The Seventh Schedule divides legislative subjects between the Union and the States into three lists: the Union List (List I), State List (List II), and Concurrent List (List III).

 

• Subjects of national importance requiring uniform policy (like railways, inter-state trade, and banking) are placed in the Union List.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other State List subjects include public order, police, public health, agriculture, and local government.

 

• The Concurrent List includes subjects like education, forests, and marriage, on which both the Centre and States can legislate.

 

NOTE

 

• Railways (Option 1): Entry 22 of the Union List — under exclusive central control.

 

• Inter-state trade and commerce (Option 3): Entry 42 of the Union List, since it concerns commerce across state boundaries.

 

• Post office saving Bank (Option 4): Falls under the Union List, given its nationwide postal/banking character.

question: As on November 2022, who is the first citizen of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Droupadi Murmu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As on November 2022, Droupadi Murmu was serving as the 15th President of India, having taken oath on 25 July 2022.

 

• The President of India is referred to as the "first citizen of India," being the ceremonial head of state and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.

 

• She succeeded Ram Nath Kovind, whose term ended on 24 July 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Droupadi Murmu is the first tribal person and the second woman to hold the office of President of India.

 

• By convention, the Vice-President is regarded as the "second citizen" and the Prime Minister as the "third citizen."

 

NOTE

 

• Sonia Gandhi (Option 1): A senior political leader (former UPA Chairperson/Congress President), not the President of India.

 

• Narendra Modi (Option 3): Prime Minister of India (head of government), not the ceremonial "first citizen."

 

• Amit Shah (Option 4): Union Home Minister of India, not the President.

question: International Women’s Day is celebrated on?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8th march.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• International Women's Day is observed every year on 8th March worldwide, celebrating the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women.

 

• It also marks a call to action for accelerating gender equality.

 

• The observance originated from labour movements in the early 20th century in North America and Europe.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The theme and campaign hashtags change every year (e.g., #BreakTheBias in 2022).

 

• The United Nations began officially observing International Women's Day from 1975 (International Women's Year).

 

NOTE

 

• 12th march (Option 1): Not the date for International Women's Day.

 

• 8th July (Option 3): Incorrect month; the correct date falls in March.

 

• 12th July (Option 4): Incorrect; 12 July is instead observed as Malala Day, unrelated to Women's Day.

question: When the grains of sand are very fine and light, the wind can carry it over very long distances. When such sand is deposited in large areas, it is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is loess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loess is a fine, wind-deposited (aeolian) sediment, typically composed of silt-sized particles, that accumulates over large areas when carried by wind over long distances (लोयस — पवन-निक्षेपित मिट्टी).

 

• Loess deposits are usually yellowish in colour and highly fertile, forming productive agricultural soils (e.g., the Loess Plateau in China).

 

• Other wind erosion/deposition landforms include sand dunes, barchans, and ripples.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Loess deposits are unstratified (lacking distinct layering) and highly porous.

 

• The Loess Plateau in China is one of the largest loess deposits in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• moraines (Option 2): Deposits of rock debris carried and left behind by glaciers, not wind.

 

• mushroom (Option 3): Refers to mushroom (pedestal) rocks, a wind-erosional landform, not a deposit of fine sand.

 

• stacks (Option 4): Isolated rock pillars formed by coastal wave erosion, unrelated to wind-blown sand deposits.

question: Hari Prasad Chaurasia is associated with which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bansuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia is a renowned Indian classical musician associated with the Bansuri (bamboo flute) (बांसुरी — पंडित हरिप्रसाद चौरसिया).

 

• He is widely credited with popularising the bansuri as a solo classical instrument in Hindustani classical music.

 

• He has received several honours, including the Padma Vibhushan (2000) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• He co-founded the Vrindaban Gurukul in Mumbai and Bhopal for teaching Indian classical music.

 

• Another celebrated bansuri player is Pandit Pannalal Ghosh.

 

NOTE

 

• Tabla (Option 2): Associated with maestros such as Zakir Hussain and Ustad Alla Rakha, not Hari Prasad Chaurasia.

 

• Drum (Option 3): A Western percussion instrument, unrelated to Hari Prasad Chaurasia.

 

• Veena (Option 4): Associated with artists such as Chitti Babu, not Hari Prasad Chaurasia.

question: According to WHO, If a person’s BMI is below 18.5 he/she is classified as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Underweight.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the World Health Organization (WHO), Body Mass Index (BMI) is calculated as weight (kg) divided by height squared (m²).

 

• A BMI below 18.5 is classified as "Underweight."

 

• BMI of 18.5–24.9 is "Normal weight," 25–29.9 is "Overweight," and 30 or above is classified as "Obese."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• BMI is a simple screening tool and does not directly measure body fat percentage or account for muscle mass.

 

• Some clinical contexts in Asian populations use slightly adjusted BMI cut-offs, but the WHO standard of below 18.5 as underweight remains the global reference.

 

NOTE

 

• Healthy (Option 1): Corresponds to a BMI range of 18.5–24.9, not below 18.5.

 

• Blind (Option 2): Unrelated to BMI classification; refers to a vision impairment.

 

• Mentally unfit (Option 4): Not a BMI category; an unrelated term.

question: Who among the following was a famous ruler of the Maratha dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (1630–1680) was the founder and most famous ruler of the Maratha Empire, crowned as Chhatrapati (sovereign) in 1674 at Raigad (छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज — मराठा साम्राज्य के संस्थापक).

 

• He established a strong, independent Maratha kingdom by resisting Mughal expansion in the Deccan and introduced an efficient administration through the Ashta Pradhan (council of eight ministers).

 

• He is renowned for his guerrilla warfare tactics and for building and capturing forts across western India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shivaji's coronation in 1674 marked the formal establishment of the Maratha Empire.

 

• Later Maratha rulers and Peshwas expanded the empire significantly, making it a dominant power in 18th-century India.

 

NOTE

 

• Porus (Option 1): An ancient Indian king who fought Alexander the Great at the Battle of the Hydaspes (326 BCE); unrelated to the Marathas.

 

• Man Singh (Option 3): A Rajput general and trusted commander of Mughal emperor Akbar, not a Maratha ruler.

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan (Option 4): The last Hindu Chahamana (Chauhan) ruler of Delhi/Ajmer, defeated by Muhammad of Ghor in 1192; unrelated to the Marathas.

question: In September 2022 at Bengaluru Space Expo (BSX) in Bengaluru, ISRO and space agency of ______ facilitated signage of half a dozen MoUs between the startups of the two countries focusing on the space tech.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022, at the Bengaluru Space Expo (BSX), ISRO and the Australian Space Agency facilitated the signing of about half a dozen (six) MoUs between space startups of India and Australia, focused on space technology collaboration.

 

• This built on growing India–Australia space cooperation, which continued with further MoUs signed at subsequent forums, such as the 2024 Bengaluru Space Expo and the Australian Space Forum.

 

• The Bengaluru Space Expo is a biennial international event showcasing India's space capabilities, organised in association with ISRO, IN-SPACe, and NSIL.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India and Australia have strengthened space ties as part of their broader strategic partnership, including cooperation in space situational awareness.

 

• The 7th edition of BSX 2022 saw participation from over 100 companies from around 15 countries.

 

NOTE

 

• France (Option 1): France's space agency (CNES) has separate long-standing cooperation with ISRO, but was not the partner in this specific BSX 2022 MoU signing.

 

• USA (Option 2): The US (NASA) collaborates with ISRO on missions like NISAR, but was not the specific partner referenced in this BSX 2022 MoU event.

 

• Israel (Option 3): Israel has cooperated with ISRO on select satellite missions, but was not the country involved in this specific BSX 2022 MoU signing.

question:
Which of the following pairs of "term – sports" is correct?
I. Eagle – Hockey
II. Penalty kick - Volleyball
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I ("Eagle – Hockey") is incorrect: "Eagle" is a golf term, referring to a score of two strokes under par on a hole.

 

• Statement II ("Penalty kick - Volleyball") is incorrect: "Penalty kick" is a term used in football (soccer) and handball, not volleyball, which instead uses terms like "kill," "dig," and "ace."

 

• Since neither statement correctly pairs the term with its sport, "Neither I nor II" is the correct response.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common hockey terms include "Bully," "Penalty corner," "Penalty stroke," and "Sixteen-yard hit."

 

• Common volleyball terms include "Rally," "Block," "Dig," and "Service ace."

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since "Eagle" is a golf term, not a hockey term.

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, since neither pairing is factually correct.

question: The book titled ‘The Ministry of Utmost Happiness’ has been written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" (2017) is a novel written by Arundhati Roy, her second novel after the Booker Prize-winning "The God of Small Things" (1997) (अरुंधति रॉय — भारतीय लेखिका).

 

• The novel is set across various locations in India and explores themes of identity, politics, and social issues over several decades.

 

• Arundhati Roy is also well known for her essays and activism on social and environmental issues.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• "The God of Small Things" won the Booker Prize in 1997, making Roy the first Indian woman to win the award.

 

• Roy has received other honours, including the Sahitya Akademi Award, which she declined in 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Jia Pingwa (Option 1): A Chinese author known for novels like "Ruined City"; unrelated to this book.

 

• Dan Brown (Option 2): American author known for thrillers like "The Da Vinci Code," not this book.
